name: Compute Express Link 4.0
bandwidth_basis: x16, PER DIRECTION, full duplex. The consortium states CXL 4.0 doubles bandwidth from 64 GT/s to 128 GT/s: 15.126 GB/s per lane per direction and 242.0 GB/s BIDIRECTIONAL AGGREGATE at x16, so the recorded per-direction value is 121 GB/s. The consortium explicitly adds 'zero added latency' for the doubling and retains the CXL 3.x 256B flit format, so this is a clean 2x of cxl-3-x per direction.
topology: Switched fabric with pooling, now with native x2 width for platform fan-out, bundled ports combining host and Type 1/2 accelerator ports, and support for up to four retimers for channel reach.
switching: Mature switched fabric. Bundled ports are the notable feature for accelerators: combining a host port with Type 1/2 device ports raises the bandwidth of one connection, which is how an accelerator-attached tier would get beyond a single x16 worth of bandwidth.
notes: Inference consequence: at 121 GB/s per direction x16 this is the first CXL generation whose per-direction rate is within ~4x of NVLink 4, and with bundled/native x2 widths it can approach NVLink class bandwidth. That still does not make it a tensor-parallel fabric: CXL's coherent model is CPU-memory-centric and it has no in-network reduction, so TP collectives over CXL pay full latency with no SHARP equivalent. The credible use is memory expansion and pooling - large-batch decode with KV cache resident in pooled CXL memory. Four retimers of channel reach matters for rack-scale placement. Consortium states full backward compatibility with 3.x, 2.0, 1.1, 1.0.
